title: Maximum Number of Jumps to Reach the Last Index
summary: Given an array nums and a target value, starting from index 0, you can jump to any index j where 0 <= i < j < n and -target <= nums[j] - nums[i] <= target.
statement: Given an array nums and a target value, starting from index 0, you can jump to any index j where 0 <= i < j < n and -target <= nums[j] - nums[i] <= target. Determine the maximum number of jumps needed to reach the last index. If reaching the last index is impossible, return -1.
constraints: Start at index zero and jump only to a larger index.
A jump i to j is allowed when abs(nums[j]-nums[i]) is at most target.
Return the maximum jumps reaching the final index, or -1 when unreachable.
hints: Let dp[j] be the maximum jumps reaching j.
For every earlier reachable i satisfying the value bound, relax dp[j] with dp[i]+1.
Return the final state or -1 if it remains negative.
Every path to j has a unique preceding index i, so considering all earlier i exhausts and maximizes valid paths.
